Children seem particularly sensitive to the adverse effects of oral tretinoin on the CNS (see also Effects on the Eyes, and Administration in Children, above). A lipid-based intravenous formulation of tretinoin is under investigation for the treatment of APL. Tretinoin has also been tried for topical chemoprevention in pa- tients at increased risk of skin cancers, and in the management of oral leucoplakia (see Malignant Neoplasms under Isotretinoin, p.1603). 1. Blood 1999; 94: 1192–1200. Skin disorders. Topical treatment with tretinoin has been tried with varying success in a wide range of cutaneous conditions. Its use in acne (p.1577) is well established. Some benefit has also been reported in rosacea1 (p.1583), in keratinisation disorders such as Darier’s disease (p.1578), and in pigmentation disorders (p.1582) such as chloasma.2 Healing of diabetic foot ulcers (see Diabetic Complications, p.433) was improved in a small place- bo-controlled study of topical tretinoin.3 The 0.05% solution was applied topically for 10 minutes of every day for 4 weeks.
